notes.1: Line 19: 'bülwesse' is obscure; 'soft' is guessed from the comparison with Mary's hair (perhaps 'blunt' or 'harmless'). 'wizzôt' (lines 40, 43) can mean 'law' or the sacrament of the altar; taken as the sacrament beside baptism and chrism. Line 26: 'scheiden' taken as exempting the sword from the blessing, so that it alone can cut.

nodes.text: may it be my shield of protection today.
The holy child of heaven bade me rise today;
in the grace of its name I will go forth today,
with the words of holy God,
so that everything may be well disposed to me
I am bold of spirit today;
today, Lord, I leap into your power.
may it be my shirt of protection today.
The weapons of all my enemies,
may they lie today and sleep,
as was the hair of my lady St Mary
and yet was a pure maiden.
May my head be of steel today;
may no kind of weapon cut into it.
I will exempt from the blessing,
so that it cuts and bites
may he be my good hauberk today, amen.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is called by the wonderful
name Tetragrammaton, and in the name of the Holy Spirit.
In honour of the name that I have named,
and in its grace I go today.
May the words be true and firm for me
with which baptism and the chrism
with that may I be blessed today
Amen. As true may this be as that our Lord God was born of St Mary while she was a maiden. Amen.
